chapter: Brawls, the Ink Spots and boyhood recollections
title: Underpaid always; Lou Irwin and the Jerome Kern show
summary: Bubbles grumbled about pay and management; after learning Lou Irwin could have won more for the Kern show he began setting his own salary.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: "What did he ever do?" "How long has he been there?" What school did he go to," all that. "He's been on Broadway" so-and-so, so-and-so. That's what did it, you know. So I wasn't displeased about nothing but one thing. I was displeased about the management and displeased about the money received for the interest put in plus the efforts extended in this profession. I've been always unhappy about that. Thought it was disgraceful. I should be a rich man, but how can I be rich when I ain't got no money. Can't be rich that way, m-m. And I've been underpaid so much
it ain't even funny. Never mind. I don't mind that because I figure I'd get it on the next job.

Lou Irwin did one for me, he booked me on a show with Jerome Kern who put on a show with all the songs he had written in Hollywood and I was one of the performers that was in it with Louis Prima and Dick Powell and Robert Montgomery and Fred Astaire, with all these people in this show. He books me in there and would you believe that the man that puts on the shows, it's like the aged father show that you put on -- he was the one that got me to my agent, but my agent don't know that I'm going to bump into this man -- I guess he knew that he was going to bump into me but when he saw me and my associates that knew me so well, this is the agent that I was telling you about that Lou Irwin had booked me through for this show. But when he saw me hanging out with these people that knew me so well and we looked like we're such a family, he came to me and says, 'You need

to get another agent. I says, "Why?" He says, "You could have got more money than what you did. You could have got better than $750 (I think it was) for this show. He just didn't fight enough for it." I says, "Really?" I says, "That's all right. I'm getting more now than what I'm doing -- for more than what I'm doing now. I'll make it up some other time to clear my point of it." But I never did tell Lou about that. I just made it from that point on that I'll set a salary for him to go by instead of him setting one. I used to let him set the salary just like I let Nat set the salary. Then he'd ask me did I want to go for it. If I don't go for it then if I need ten or fifteen or twenty dollars or a hundred dollars, he's not going to turn down it down that day. See what I'm saying?
So that was the only thing that I went along with that I changed after this incident happened.
So now when you speak about

salary, that's why I go and let this girl book me in this show because she didn't know enough about the salary. She don't know what California is, she don't know about agencies neither. So I didn't want her to mess with this idea of booking me in that show. So I said do it through whats'name because he knows, because she worked for Lou Irwin and Lou Irwin knew what to do where I was concerned and I figured she knows the same thing. She's a good agent. She's a good agent. Very good.
